title: Chapter 1886: Loose Ends Settled (II)
content:
Chapter 1886: Loose Ends Settled (II)

Li Ximing watched him through narrowed eyes as Xianyao said softly, "My forebears came from Guanlong and received Wei's kindness. I am not Situ Huo, who can disregard his ancestors entirely, and thus I had to say something. If my words displease you, Daoist Master, then for the sake of a dying man... forgive this old fellow..."

With a word of farewell, he turned and departed on the wind. Beside him, Chengqian plainly did not know whether to leave or stay. Deeply embarrassed, he apologized repeatedly. "He is old and says some muddled things. Please do not take them to heart, senior!"

Li Ximing nodded. "They were all sincere words. I have learned from them!"

With a complicated expression, Chengqian cupped his hands and hurried after his master. Catching up with him in the great void, he sighed. "Master, why put yourself through this?"

His master remained silent. Knowing this was not the place to talk, Chengqian held back until they reached their own mountain gate, where clouds drifted around a suspended immortal mountain.

Only then did he say urgently, "Tianwu had the Wanlin Upper Sect, and the Lin and Li Families to conquer lands, eradicate evil, and impose order everywhere on his behalf. Even their own people accused Wanlin of wanting to become a second Thunder Palace. Now, naturally, there is a King of Wei to fill that role. That must be the purpose behind the [Heavenly Nurturing Urn]. Both sides are willing... Why must you involve yourself, master?"

Xianyao's expression grew downcast. He stood silently for a long while, hands behind his back, before lowering his eyes. "Why? I may have my own motives, but the King of Wei cannot succeed! How will it end for him? Can I not even offer a word of advice?"

Chengqian knew that his master understood everything, and was merely being stubborn. "Since you mentioned the Situ Family, master, I must say something too. How illustrious were they under Wei? They held the title of King Shouyi and were ranked among Guanlong's great clans. And what are they doing now? Why torment yourself over old ties? Looking after Situ Huo all these years was one thing. Why involve yourself in this as well?"

The old man sat down. "I know I should stay out of it. But hearing all those rumors, I could not rest without saying something. In the end, I had to speak. Li Ximing is not someone who fails to recognize good intentions. Enough, enough. Just think of it as an old man with little time left earning you some goodwill!"

Chengqian sighed deeply and fell silent.

————

After seeing Sima Yuanli off, Li Ximing wasted no time in summoning Li Jiangzong to hear the family's news in detail. This direct descendant of the first lineage had grown increasingly adept over the years he had spent managing clan affairs.

He bowed before the courtyard and reported each matter in turn. "...Yusui is now being looked after by Suihuan. Third Brother also visited once... Apparently, he had been ordered to return to court with his troops. He stopped by the lake, but neither of you was here...

"There is one other matter... While you were both away, two cultivators became ready to break through. The first is Suikuan, a direct descendant of our family. He is waiting in the mountains."

After hearing his full report, Li Ximing raised his brows. "Good news! The Suiyu generation is gradually coming into its own. He is Suining's brother, isn't he? Have him come up so I can meet him."

Li Jiangzong respectfully withdrew. Soon, a young man came up from the mountain. He had a round face and fine eyebrows. Though not particularly handsome, he looked well behaved.

Bowing with both hands pressed to the ground, he said respectfully, "Greetings, Daoist Master!"

"Rise." Li Ximing looked him over. "You cultivate [Upper Rite]?"

"Yes, Daoist Master."

Though they were brothers, Li Suikuan was entirely different from Li Suining in both appearance and temperament. The formation prodigy was cold and even somewhat melancholy, always seeming to harbor countless worries. Li Suikuan, however, was clear-minded with a resolute gaze.

Li Ximing nodded inwardly and thought,

He is single-minded. After all these years of Minggong helping the Eastern Residence nurture its juniors, it has finally produced two pillars.

He committed the name to memory, bestowed spirit pills upon him, and smiled. "Since you are entering seclusion, have you made any plans for after your breakthrough? It is rare for the Eastern Residence to produce talents like you and your brother. You deserve a proper reward."

Li Suikuan bowed. "I do not wish to receive rewards without merit. If fortune allows me to succeed, I ask only to march north with the army, bearing a saber and raising your royal banner."

Li Ximing was genuinely taken aback. He studied the young man again, as he brushed the pad of his index finger. An almost imperceptible gleam flashed at his fingertip.

Utterly sincere...

For the first time, a direct descendant of the Li Family was willing to abandon their comfortable life at the lake and explicitly ask to head north. Li Ximing sighed inwardly, unable to say whether he felt joy or sorrow.

After a moment's silence, he said, "Very well. Once you emerge from seclusion, go and see Zhouda."

Li Suikuan respectfully took his leave and excitedly hurried down. No longer in the mood to ask further questions, Li Ximing stepped into the great void and departed, descending within his family's great formation.

The purple-and-gold hall remained dark as he arrived on the wind. Li Zhouwei sat quietly in the main seat, his legs crossed and both hands held before his dantian. A pill shaped like a golden cicada rested in his palms. He seemed to be cultivating a divine ability.

The balance of Yin and Yang offered little benefit to [Severed Crimson Arrowhead], so Li Zhouwei had remained here to cultivate with the [Setting Sun Armor-Sundering Pill] in his hands.

Opening his golden eyes, he immediately noticed his visitor's troubled mood and smiled. "Granduncle, what is troubling you...?"

Li Ximing sighed and replied, "We have become thoroughly entangled in Shehu's affairs. Now it seems the gains and troubles are evenly matched. Sometimes I wonder whether we might have been better off without this [Heavenly Nurturing Urn]."

Li Zhouwei shook his head. Knowing this elder was easily swayed, he suspected someone had said something to him. He merely said with a smile, "Without the [Heavenly Nurturing Urn], we would still have no idea where that spirit root came from! There is no turning back. We must find our way forward with each step. Dealing with Shehu has settled a matter of great importance.

"The hardest one is dealt with. We have ample justification for acting against those beasts in the southern border next. You see this as a bad thing, granduncle... I see it as a good thing."

His faint smile put Li Ximing at ease. Daoist Master Zhaojing pondered for a long while, then exhaled. "I really should not take up more of your time. Since you are cultivating here, you can keep an eye on the lake as well. I still need to attend to your weapon."

"Thank you, granduncle."

Li Zhouwei nodded and watched him dissolve into light. His golden eyes closed once more, and the hall immediately dimmed. Only the pill between his palms pulsed faintly, giving off a gentle red glow.
